Reference / compression/state

compression/state#

Stateful streaming codecs: writes may produce no output until a later write or finish().

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

codec.write([byte(1), byte(2)]);
codec.finish();
let batch = codec.output();
batch.bytes(1); // drain the remainder before dropping this batch
codec.close();

Description#

Stateful streaming codecs: writes may produce no output until a later write or finish(). finish() flushes pending output and marks successful completion. Writing (including empty input) or finishing after completion is InvalidState. close() is idempotent, discards unclaimed output and never implies finish(). Only close()/closed() remain valid after close. Concrete owners need destroy. A data/codec failure permits only closing; invalid arguments do not consume.

output() TRANSFERS currently available bytes as an independent finite Reading. Its EOF is permanent: it is a batch, not the live codec output queue. Empty batches before finished() do not mean the codec reached EOF. Drain/retain each batch before dropping it; subsequent output() calls transfer only new bytes. A transferred batch survives closing its codec and owns its own lifetime.

The role fakes echo bytes; they are not codecs. The compressor delays output until finish. The decompressor emits immediately with an eight-byte cumulative limit and empty remainder after finish. Each fake has its own typed state.

object CompressionOutput#

object CompressionOutput does Reading, Closing

Finite owned output batch. Reading requires limit > 0, is consuming, and stays at EOF once empty. Invalid limits do not consume bytes. close()/destroy release the private buffer; close is idempotent and reads after close fail. Input and returned byte arrays are independent of this resource's lifetime.

object DecompressionBudget#

object DecompressionBudget

Immutable cumulative output allowance. The codec retains each spent() result; reading output must never reset it. Maximum is positive, amount nonnegative. Spending checks remaining capacity before subtraction (no overflowing sum). Zero spending succeeds; excess/negative spending leaves the receiver intact. Example: DecompressionBudget(8).spent(3).remaining() == 5. No owned resources.
